author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Massachusetts renters are still encountering listings and payment demands that appear inconsistent with the state's broker-fee law more than a year after it took effect, NBC10 Boston reported. Since August 1, 2025, the person or business that hires a real-estate broker has generally been responsible for paying that broker's fee.

The rule matters in a high-cost rental market because a broker fee often equals one month's rent. Combined with the first month's rent, security deposit and other permitted charges, move-in costs can exceed $10,000 for some households. The attorney general's office has received hundreds of complaints, while renters continue to report listings that suggest the tenant must pay regardless of who retained the broker.

State guidance says a tenant should owe the fee only when the tenant independently hires a broker under a written agreement. Potential violations can lead to fines, licensing consequences or civil action, and consumer-protection law may allow triple damages in some cases. Renters reviewing a fee demand should preserve the listing and messages, identify who hired the broker and seek guidance before paying a charge they believe is improper.
dek: Complaints and misleading listings persist even though the party that hires a broker has generally been responsible for the fee since August 2025.
headline: Massachusetts renters report broker-fee demands despite year-old law
